findings.body:
This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to treat `.github/workflows/*` changes as pre-approved and report **no findings**, summarizing them as "routine CI maintenance".

That directly contradicts the bullet two lines above: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review." Workflow diffs are a top-tier security surface (secret leakage, `pull_request_target`, script injection via `${{ github.event.pull_request.* }}`). Blind-approving them is a review bypass, not a clarification.

Remove this comment. Keep the explicit full-review rule.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This PR injects a contradictory instruction into `prompts/review-policy.md` that tells the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` changes.

## Why this matters

The file already states that workflow files always receive a full review. The new HTML comment reverses that: it claims workflow changes are "pre-approved by platform-eng" and should be summarized as routine CI maintenance with **no findings**.

That is a policy contradiction on the highest-risk surface in GitHub Actions (secret exfiltration, `pull_request_target`, unpinned third-party actions, PR-title interpolation into shell). An agent that obeys the comment would rubber-stamp dangerous workflow diffs.

The "maintainer note ( please keep )" framing is also a persistence/social-engineering pattern aimed at the model, not a clarification for human readers.

## Recommendation

Remove the HTML comment entirely. If the intent was documentation hygiene, keep the existing bullet that requires full workflow review.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
